== Introduction ==

Domoticz supports visual themes that let you change the look of the web interface without modifying core files.

The active theme is configured in '''Setup → Settings → System → GUI theme''' and defaults to <code>default</code>.

=== How URL rewriting works ===

<code>index.html</code> always loads <code>styles/default/custom.css</code>. The Domoticz web server (cWebem) intercepts every request for a file under <code>styles/default/</code> and transparently serves the corresponding file from the active theme folder if it exists there. If the file does not exist in the active theme folder, the request falls through to <code>styles/default/</code>.

This means:
* A theme only needs to provide files it actually overrides.
* <code>common.css</code>, <code>variables.css</code>, and <code>legacy.css</code> are served from <code>default/</code> unless your theme provides its own copies.
* Fallback is per-file — you can override <code>dark.css</code> alone without touching anything else.

== Minimum required files ==

Every theme needs exactly one file: '''custom.css'''.

=== Dark theme ===

<source lang="css">
@import url("../../css/legacy.css"); /* required */
@import url("common.css");           /* shared utilities — served from default/ via fallback */
@import url("dark.css");             /* your dark :root overrides */
</source>

=== Light theme ===

<source lang="css">
@import url("../../css/legacy.css"); /* required */
@import url("common.css");           /* shared utilities — light by default, no dark.css needed */
</source>

For a light theme you do not need a <code>dark.css</code>. The <code>--dz-*</code> variable defaults defined in <code>variables.css</code> are light-valued, so form controls, modals, and buttons render correctly without any <code>:root</code> override block.

== CSS load order ==

The following shows the full waterfall from <code>index.html</code> to theme variables. Theme authors need to understand what loads when and which <code>:root</code> block wins.

<pre>
index.html  →  <link> files loaded in parallel:
  css/style.css                        (structural resets + body { background: var(--dz-body-bg) })
  css/bootstrap.css
  css/bootstrap-responsive.css
  ... other lib CSS ...
  styles/default/custom.css            (last <link>; server-rewritten to active theme)
    └─ @import legacy.css              (serial fetch 1)
    │    └─ @import variables.css        (serial fetch 2 — --dz-* light defaults + widget rules)
    ├─ @import common.css              (serial fetch 3 — colour-neutral utilities)
    ├─ @import dark.css                (serial fetch 4 — dark :root overrides, dark themes only)
    └─ theme's own :root block         (inline in custom.css — wins by source order)
</pre>

=== What wins (specificity rules) ===

* All <code>:root</code> blocks have the same specificity <code>(0,1,0)</code> — '''last one wins''' by source order.
* <code>variables.css</code> <code>:root</code> loads first → <code>dark.css</code> <code>:root</code> overrides it → theme's inline <code>:root</code> overrides that.
* For non-variable rules, normal CSS specificity applies.
* Inline styles from JavaScript (<code>$(el).css(...)</code>) override everything, including variables.

== CSS variable reference ==

All <code>--dz-*</code> variables are defined in <code>css/variables.css</code> with light values as their defaults. These variables form the stable public theming API.

The default Domoticz theme uses light widget colours on a dark page background. <code>default/dark.css</code> provides the dark body gradient, dark form controls, modals, buttons, and content panels. Widget card colours are intentionally left at the light defaults from <code>variables.css</code>.

The '''"Suggested dark value"''' column in the tables below shows recommended values for theme authors building a fully dark theme. They are not defined anywhere by default — you must set them yourself in your theme's <code>:root</code> block or <code>dark.css</code>.

== Creating a dark theme ==

Place variable overrides in a <code>dark.css</code> file in your theme folder and import it from <code>custom.css</code>:

'''custom.css:'''

<source lang="css">
@import url("../../css/legacy.css");
@import url("common.css");
@import url("dark.css");
</source>

'''dark.css:'''

<source lang="css">
:root {
  --dz-widget-bg:          #1e2a3a;
  --dz-widget-text:        #f0f0f0;
  --dz-widget-name-bg:     #2a3a50;
  --dz-widget-name-border: #3a4a60;
  --dz-widget-name-text:   #f0f0f0;
  --dz-widget-hover-bg:    #253040;
  --dz-widget-hover-name-bg: #354558;

  --dz-status-normal:      #283750;
  --dz-status-protected:   #354a80;
  --dz-status-timeout:     #8b1a23;
  --dz-status-low-battery: #7a7a00;
  --dz-status-disabled:    #4a4a4a;

  --dz-body-bg:            #0f1a2a;
  --dz-body-text:          #f0f0f0;
  --dz-input-bg:           #1a2a3a;
  --dz-input-text:         #ddd;
  --dz-input-border:       #3a4a5a;
  --dz-modal-bg:           #1e2a3a;
  --dz-modal-text:         #f0f0f0;
  --dz-modal-header-bg:    #152030;
}

body {
  background: var(--dz-body-bg);
  color: var(--dz-body-text);
}
</source>

== Creating a light theme ==

For a light theme, import <code>common.css</code> only — no <code>dark.css</code>. The <code>--dz-*</code> defaults in <code>variables.css</code> are already light-valued, so widgets render correctly without a full <code>:root</code> override block. You only need to override the variables you want to change.

The one variable you '''must''' override is <code>--dz-body-bg</code>, because its default (<code>#202020</code>) is intentionally dark to prevent FOUC.

'''custom.css:'''

<source lang="css">
@import url("../../css/legacy.css");
@import url("common.css");

:root {
  --dz-widget-bg:   #e8f0f8;   /* optional: fine-tune widget colour */
  --dz-body-bg:     #f0f2f5;   /* required: override the dark FOUC default */
  --dz-body-text:   #333;
}

body {
  background: var(--dz-body-bg);
  color: var(--dz-body-text);
}
</source>

== Variable contract versioning ==

The <code>--dz-*</code> variables defined in <code>variables.css</code> and <code>common.css</code> are the stable public API for theme authors.

{| class="wikitable"
! Change type !! Policy
|-
| Adding new variables || Safe — themes that do not reference them are unaffected
|-
| Changing default values || Safe with a release note — themes that override the variable are unaffected; themes relying on the default will see the change
|-
| Renaming or removing a variable || Requires a deprecation window. The old name is kept as an alias (<code>--dz-old-name: var(--dz-new-name)</code>) for at least two releases
|-
| Internal CSS selectors and class names || May change between releases without compatibility guarantees — use <code>--dz-*</code> variables instead of targeting selectors
|}

== Community theme migration guide ==

If your theme was built before the CSS variable system was introduced, it likely contains long selector chains targeting internal widget tables. These can now be replaced with a single <code>:root</code> block.

=== Before (old approach) ===

<source lang="css">
/* Fighting legacy.css specificity to change widget colours */
body table#itemtablesmall tbody tr          { background-color: #1e2a3a !important; }
body table#itemtabledoubleicon tbody tr     { background-color: #1e2a3a !important; }
/* ... repeated 8 times for every table variant ... */
body table#itemtablesmall tbody tr td:first-child { background-color: #2a3a50 !important; }
/* ... repeated 8 times again ... */
</source>

=== After (new approach) ===

<source lang="css">
/* One :root block replaces all of the above */
:root {
  --dz-widget-bg:      #1e2a3a;
  --dz-widget-name-bg: #2a3a50;
}
</source>

=== Migration checklist ===

# Remove all <code>body table#itemtable*</code> colour overrides from your theme.
# Replace them with a <code>:root { --dz-*: your-values; }</code> block.
# Review <code>!important</code> declarations on widget colour properties — most are now unnecessary.
# If your theme copied rules from <code>legacy.css</code>, remove those copies — they will conflict with the variable-driven rules.

== Theme author guidelines ==

* '''Prefer variable overrides''' over selector chains. Changing <code>--dz-widget-bg</code> is safer and more forward-compatible than targeting <code>.item</code> or <code>table#itemtablesmall</code>.
* '''Do not override Bootstrap layout globally.''' Overriding <code>.row-fluid</code>, <code>.span*</code>, or <code>.container-fluid</code> at the top level breaks page structure. Scope overrides to specific containers.
* '''Scope custom selectors.''' Target <code>#holder .item</code> rather than bare <code>.item</code>, to avoid interfering with modals and other contexts.
* '''Do not use <code>!important</code> on variable-driven properties.''' It defeats the purpose of the variable contract and makes your overrides impossible for downstream themes to fix.
* '''Do not import extras_and_animations.css by default''' unless your theme explicitly wants transitions and hover animations. When you do want them, add <code>@import url("extras_and_animations.css");</code> to your <code>custom.css</code>.

== Button systems ==

Domoticz has three separate button systems. Theme authors need to be aware of all three:

{| class="wikitable"
! System !! Classes !! Used where
|-
| Bootstrap 2.x || <code>.btn</code>, <code>.btn-default</code>, <code>.btn-primary</code>, <code>.btn-warning</code>, <code>.btn-danger</code>, <code>.btn-info</code>, <code>.btn-success</code> || Modal footers, toolbar actions, device overview
|-
| Custom Domoticz || <code>.btnstyle</code>, <code>.btnstylerev</code>, <code>.btnstyle3</code>, <code>.btnstyle3-sel</code>, <code>.btnstyle3-dis</code> || Switches tab, scene buttons
|-
| Small action || <code>.btnsmall</code>, <code>.btnsmall-sel</code>, <code>.btn-mini</code> || Device options menus, log/timer tabs
|}

The <code>--dz-btn-*</code> variables control Bootstrap <code>.btn*</code> styles. The <code>.btnstyle*</code> and <code>.btnsmall*</code> systems do not yet have variables — override them with explicit selectors if needed.

== Theme settings storage ==

Themes can persist their own configuration in the Domoticz database without using user variables. Settings are stored per theme, in two layers:

* '''Instance defaults''': one set per installation, writable by admins. These act as the defaults every user starts from.
* '''Per-user overlay''': one set per user account, writable by any authenticated user (including Viewer rights) for their own account only. When a user has an overlay for a theme, it replaces the instance defaults for that theme entirely (the merge is per theme name, not per key inside the theme's object).

Requires a core whose <code>getversion</code> response contains <code>ThemeSettingsAPI: 1</code> (see below); older cores return HTTP 400 for the new commands.

=== Reading settings ===

<code>getsettings</code> returns a <code>ThemeSettings</code> object whose top-level keys are theme names, resolved for the calling user: the instance defaults overlaid with the caller's own per-user values. Themes that already read <code>data.ThemeSettings[THEME_NAME]</code> keep working unchanged and get per-user values for free.

<source lang="javascript">
var THEME_NAME = 'YourTheme';   // must match the folder name under www/styles/

$.getJSON('json.htm?type=command&param=getsettings', function (data) {
    var settings = (data.ThemeSettings && data.ThemeSettings[THEME_NAME]) || {};
    // apply settings...
});
</source>

On the Settings page the same merged object is exposed as <code>$scope.ThemeSettings</code>.

To inspect the two layers separately (for example to label options as "default" vs "yours"), use <code>themesettings_get</code>:

<source lang="text">
json.htm?type=command&param=themesettings_get&theme=YourTheme
</source>

The response contains an <code>instance</code> and a <code>user</code> object, each with <code>present</code> (boolean), and when present <code>value</code> (the stored object) and <code>lastupdate</code> (a token needed for writing, see below). It also contains <code>PerUser</code> (see Known limitations).

=== Writing settings ===

Two POST commands write settings. Both take the theme name as an explicit <code>theme</code> parameter and the settings as a <code>value</code> parameter holding a JSON object.

* <code>themesettings_set</code>: writes the calling user's own overlay. Available to every authenticated user, Viewer included. There is no way to address another user's settings.
* <code>themesettings_setdefault</code>: writes the instance defaults. Admin only.

<source lang="javascript">
var THEME_NAME = 'YourTheme';

function saveThemeSettings(newSettings, lastupdate) {
    return $.post('json.htm?type=command&param=themesettings_set', {
        theme: THEME_NAME,
        value: JSON.stringify(newSettings),
        lastupdate: lastupdate || ''
    });
}
</source>

Concurrency: every stored row carries a <code>lastupdate</code> token, returned by <code>themesettings_get</code> and by every successful write. Pass the token you last read back with the write. If the row changed in the meantime the write is rejected with <code>error: "conflict"</code>; re-read, merge, and retry. Omit the token only when no row exists yet.

To remove a layer, POST with <code>reset=true</code> instead of a value. Resetting the user overlay returns that user to the instance defaults. The reset is unconditional and idempotent: it does not take a <code>lastupdate</code> token, and resetting a layer that already has no stored row succeeds without error. Store only deliberate overrides in the overlay, and offer users a reset control, otherwise their first save detaches them from instance defaults permanently.

Error reporting: failed writes return a machine-readable <code>error</code> field (<code>invalid_theme</code>, <code>missing_value</code>, <code>invalid_json</code>, <code>too_large</code>, <code>too_many_themes</code>, <code>conflict</code>, <code>post_required</code>, <code>no_identity</code>, <code>db_error</code>) plus a human-readable <code>message</code>.

=== Storage limits ===

A stored value is limited to 16 KB per theme per layer, measured on the reserialized JSON. Each layer also has a row-count cap: a user's overlay can hold settings for at most 32 themes, and the instance defaults are capped at 32 themes as well; writing a new theme name past that limit returns <code>error: "too_many_themes"</code> (updating a theme you already have settings for is unaffected). The value must be a JSON object at the root. Do not store binary data or per-device state here.

Freeing quota: hitting the cap never blocks themes you already store settings for, only new theme names. To free slots, reset the rows of themes you no longer use: the top-level keys of <code>ThemeSettings</code> in <code>getsettings</code> list every theme that has a row for you, <code>themesettings_get</code> tells you per theme whether the <code>user</code> layer is yours (<code>present: true</code>), and a POST of <code>themesettings_set</code> with <code>reset=true</code> for that theme deletes the row. Admins free instance-layer slots the same way through <code>themesettings_setdefault</code>.

=== Known limitations ===

On installations using trusted networks (<code>WebLocalNetworks</code>) or <code>-nowwwpwd</code>, every request without an explicit login resolves to the same admin identity, so all devices on the LAN share one "per-user" overlay. <code>themesettings_get</code> returns <code>PerUser: false</code> for such sessions; hide per-user options when it is false. Sessions from an explicit login return <code>PerUser: true</code> even on trusted networks.

Sessions that do not map to a user account (OAuth application tokens, access tokens) cannot store an overlay; <code>themesettings_set</code> refuses them with <code>error: "no_identity"</code>.

=== Getting the active theme name ===

<code>$scope.WebTheme</code> holds the name of the currently active theme (the folder name under <code>www/styles/</code>). Your theme's <code>custom.js</code> already knows its own name, so hardcoding it is fine.

=== Example: per-user dark/light mode toggle ===

<source lang="javascript">
var THEME_NAME = 'YourTheme';
var DEFAULTS = { style: 'dark' };
var lastToken = '';

function loadSettings(apply) {
    $.getJSON('json.htm?type=command&param=themesettings_get&theme=' + THEME_NAME, function (data) {
        var layer = (data.user && data.user.present) ? data.user : data.instance;
        lastToken = (data.user && data.user.present) ? data.user.lastupdate : '';
        apply(Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, (layer && layer.value) || {}));
    });
}

function setStyle(style) {
    var settings = Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, { style: style });
    $.post('json.htm?type=command&param=themesettings_set', {
        theme: THEME_NAME,
        value: JSON.stringify(settings),
        lastupdate: lastToken
    }, function (data) {
        if (data.status === 'OK') lastToken = data.lastupdate;
        else if (data.error === 'conflict') loadSettings(function () {});
    });
}
</source>

== Known styling limitations ==

These items are '''not''' controlled by <code>--dz-*</code> variables:

* '''JavaScript <code>.css()</code> calls''' — there are many <code>$(el).css(...)</code> calls across the frontend that apply inline styles directly to DOM elements. Inline styles have specificity <code>(1,0,0,0)</code> and override any stylesheet rule, including variable-driven ones. Some elements will not respond to variable overrides.
* '''<code>extras_and_animations.css</code>''' — imported only by the <code>default</code> theme via <code>custom.css</code>. To include transitions and hover effects in your theme, add <code>@import url("extras_and_animations.css");</code> to your <code>custom.css</code>. The file is served from <code>default/extras_and_animations.css</code> via fallback if your theme does not provide one.
* '''Hardcoded colours in other CSS files''' — <code>css/style.css</code>, <code>css/bootstrap.css</code>, and <code>css/demo_table_jui.css</code> contain many hardcoded colours that are not yet variablized.
* '''SVG icon colours''' — icon-specific colours in some device SVGs may still be hardcoded and will not respond to <code>--dz-status-*</code> overrides.

== Browser support ==

CSS custom properties (<code>var()</code>) require:

* Chrome 49+
* Firefox 31+
* Safari 9.1+
* Edge 16+

<code>display: contents</code> (used on widget custom elements) had Safari accessibility issues until Safari 16. Older browser support is not a goal for the Domoticz web UI.

== Directory structure ==

A theme lives in a subdirectory of <code>www/styles/</code>:

<pre>
www/styles/
  your-theme/
    custom.css        (required — theme entry point, loaded by index.html via cWebem rewrite)
    common.css        (optional — overrides default/common.css for this theme)
    dark.css          (optional — dark :root overrides, imported from custom.css)
    base.css          (optional — overrides default/base.css for backward compatibility)
    extras_and_animations.css  (optional — transitions and hover effects)
    images/           (optional — theme-specific images)
    fonts/            (optional — custom fonts)
</pre>

== Browser cache ==

The web frontend is configured for browser caching to speed up application launch time, which is especially useful when creating a home-screen shortcut on a mobile device.

When developing or experimenting with a theme, be sure to perform a hard reload after each change to ensure the browser fetches the latest CSS rather than serving a cached copy.

* Windows/Linux: <code>Ctrl+Shift+R</code>
* macOS: <code>Cmd+Shift+R</code>

Because the cWebem URL rewriting is transparent to the browser, switching themes in Settings does not automatically invalidate cached copies of <code>common.css</code> or <code>variables.css</code>. A full hard reload is always required after a theme switch.
